items.title: Definition 10.1.1 (2017: 10.1), equivalences and the class $E$

book.label: §10.1, Definition 10.1.1, p. 461 (2017: Definition 10.1, p. 333)
book.statement: An equivalence $F : X \to Y$ of ep-groupoids is an sc-smooth functor which is faithful and full, induces a homeomorphism $|F| : |X| \to |Y|$, and is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects; $E$ is the class of equivalences.

lean.statement: A structure on an sc-smooth functor with four fields: full, faithful, $|F|$ a homeomorphism, $F$ a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects. The class `EP.equivalences` contains the identities and is closed under composition; an equivalence is essentially surjective, and the functor from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point is an equivalence.

chips: witness: pair groupoid of ℤ → point
diff: Full and faithful are stated on the sets of morphisms $x \to x'$, as in the text, and shown equal to Mathlib's notions for the underlying functor (Findings, Chapter 10, item 1).

items.title: Lemma 10.1.2 (2017: 10.1) and the remarks around it

book.label: §10.1, Lemma 10.1.2, p. 462 (2017: Lemma 10.1, p. 334)
book.statement: An sc-smooth functor which is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects and an equivalence of categories is an equivalence; equivalences need not be invertible as functors.

lean.statement: An sc-smooth functor is an equivalence if and only if it is an equivalence of categories and a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects. $|F|$ is injective for $F$ full, surjective iff $F$ is essentially surjective, continuous, and open when $F$ is open on objects; composites of equivalences are equivalences; the equivalence from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point has no left inverse on objects.

diff: The lemma is proved with its converse; the orbit map is shown bijective, continuous and open. "Not invertible" is witnessed by an equivalence with no left inverse on objects.

items.title: Proposition 10.1.3 (2017: 10.1), the refinement $X_{\mathcal U}$

book.label: §10.1, Proposition 10.1.3, p. 462 (2017: Proposition 10.1, p. 334)
book.statement: For an open covering $\mathcal U$ of the object M-polyfold of $X$, the ep-groupoid $X_{\mathcal U}$ of pairs $(U, x)$ and triples $(U, \varphi, V)$, with the structure induced from $X$ and $\mathbf X$, and the functor $(U, x) \mapsto x$, $(U, \varphi, V) \mapsto \varphi$ is an equivalence.

lean.statement: For a covering of $X$ by open sets $U_i$ indexed by a type $\iota$ and a nonempty object set, $X_{\mathcal U}$ (objects an open subset of $\iota \times X$, morphisms an open subset of $(\iota \times \iota) \times \mathbf X$, discrete $\iota$) is an ep-groupoid and the projection $F : X_{\mathcal U} \to X$ is an equivalence; for $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ and a two-set covering it is not injective on objects.

diff: The covering is indexed by a type; the object set is assumed nonempty for the open-subset M-polyfold structure of Part I (trivial otherwise); the properness is proved with ultrafilters; the printed $(U, \varphi, v)$ is read $(U, \varphi, V)$ (Findings, Chapter 10, item 2).

items.title: Definition 10.1.4 (2017: 10.2), natural equivalence

book.label: §10.1, Definition 10.1.4, p. 463 (2017: Definition 10.2, p. 335)
book.statement: A natural transformation $\tau : F \to G$ of sc-smooth functors is an sc-smooth $\tau : X \to \mathbf Y$ with $\tau(x) : F(x) \to G(x)$ and $\tau(x') \circ F(\varphi) = G(\varphi) \circ \tau(x)$; $F \simeq G$ is an equivalence relation compatible with composition.

lean.statement: Chapter 8's `EpNatTrans` and `NaturallyEquivalent`: $\simeq$ is an equivalence relation, compatible with composition on the left and on the right; a natural transformation is a natural isomorphism of the underlying functors.

diff: The definition is Chapter 8's (Definition 8.1.13) (Findings, Chapter 10, item 3).

items.title: Proposition 10.1.5 (2017: 10.2), natural equivalence preserves equivalences

book.label: §10.1, Proposition 10.1.5, p. 464 (2017: Proposition 10.2, p. 336)
book.statement: If $F \simeq G$ and one of them is an equivalence, so is the other (quoted from the literature without proof).

lean.statement: If $F \simeq G$, then $F$ is an equivalence if and only if $G$ is.

diff: The text quotes the result without proof; it is proved: $\tau$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism since $s \circ \tau = F$, so $t \circ \tau = G$ is one on objects (Findings, Chapter 10, item 4).
